business_scope.primary_industry_name: Professional Multilingual Translation and Media Dubbing

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (with elements of Common Law influence in commercial and financial practices)

Luxembourg-US Double Tax Treaty (1996, as amended by 2009 Protocol)
Convention on Mutual Administrative Assistance in Tax Matters (MCAAT, as amended 2018)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing (as amended, including by the Law of 25 March 2020 transposing AMLD5); Grand Ducal Regulation of 1 February 2010; CSSF Regulation 12-02 (for CSSF-supervised entities); Law of 13 January 2019 establishing the Register of Beneficial Owners (Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs, 'RBE'); Law of 23 July 2016 on the SCSp (amending the Law of 10 August 1915 on commercial companies).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National Passport Authority of the Beneficial Owner's Country of Residence

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation and Good Standing of the corporate General Partner (if applicable)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registry of Commerce and Companies (RCSL) or equivalent foreign company registry

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Non-Existence of Tax Domicile / Tax Residency Certificate of the SCSp (to be obtained post-incorporation, notarized)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Luxembourg Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) / Administration des Contributions Directes (ACD)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Internal administrative issuance — no apostille required

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter for each Limited Partner (Commanditaire) contributing funds
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization if originating from a non-Hague signatory country; otherwise Hague Apostille

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory first-level and outsourced second-level screening against the Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons (SDN) list, the United Nations Security Council Consolidated Sanctions List, the European Union Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, and the Luxembourg domestic sanctions list maintained by Le Comité de suivi des sanctions financières (CSFF) of the Ministry of Finance. Politically Exposed Persons (PEP) screening (domestic, foreign, family members, and close associates) is required in accordance with Article 3(3) of the Law of 12 November 2004. Ongoing transaction monitoring and enhanced due diligence (EDD) apply when the translation agency will be managed through third-party payment rails (Wise B2B and Payoneer) not licensed as credit institutions in Luxembourg.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registration Portal of the Luxembourg Business Registers (Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés — LBR/RCSL), accessible via https://www.lbr.lu and the e-justice platform (https://e-justice.lbr.lu)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be in compliance with Luxembourg administrative languages (French, German, and Luxembourgish may be used; other languages such as English are permitted provided no translation/transliteration conflicts arise). The SCSp name must be preceded or followed by the words 'Société en Commandite Spéciale' or the abbreviation 'SCSp' and may include a registered brand/commercial name linked to the ISIC 7490 translation and media dubbing business. For non-Latin-script names, the RCSL requires a transliterated Latin-script version of the full legal name.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: ONG / ONG-Organisation non gouvernementale without prior authorization
Translation / Media (only permitted if the business indeed commits to ISIC 7490 localization activities)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: In the event of a rejection by the RCSL, an administrative appeal (recours hiérarchique) must be filed within 30 days from notification with the Minister of Justice via the Director of the Registre de Commerce, attaching the original rejection decision, a justification letter demonstrating compliance with public order rules, and proposed amendments. If the Ministerial remedy is rejected or time-barred, an appeal to the Tribunal Administratif (Administrative Court) must be initiated within 3 months under Article 27 of the Law of 21 June 1999 (procedure of administrative gazetting). Independent of the appeal, the applicant may immediately file a corrected name registration for 29 additional days of validity reserved only for new, distinct name combinations.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office addresses are NOT permissible as the registered office (siège social) of an SCSp in Luxembourg for the purposes of the Law of 10 August 1915 (Article 155-1 et seq.); however, an outsourced corporate-administration provider (domiciliation agent) approved by the CSSF or the Ministry of Justice may be used to provide a compliant single-or-multi-tenant physical registered office. For the ISIC 7490 localization agency, full physical presence is not statutorily required for the entire workforce, but the SCSp must maintain real management substance — evidenced by general partner meetings and the domiciliation agreement with the authorized corporate domiciliation agent.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Medium (35–45% inspection probability within the first 18 months). The CSSF and the Administration des contributions directes (ACD) perform targeted on-site inspections on corporate domiciliation agents and financial intermediaries; the SCSp may be drawn into such inspection for headcount and substance questionnaires, but stand-alone unannounced inspections of a translation agency registered as a low-risk SCSp remain rare. Luxembourg's RBE and beneficial ownership enforcement (Law of 13 January 2019) materially increases likelihood of documentary verification checks.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Luxembourg law of 10 August 1915 on commercial companies, as amended (Law of 1915), Article 27-1 et seq. (governing the Société en Commandite Spéciale, introduced by the Law of 11 July 2013 on partnerships); Law of 19 December 2002 on the Trade and Companies Register (RCS) and on accounting records; Law of 13 January 2019 establishing the Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), operated by the Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR), Luxembourg City; notarial filings are also transmitted by Luxembourg notaries.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of association / partnership agreement (contrat de société) executed in notarial or private deed form, filed as the acte de constitution with the RCS, followed by a legal notice in the Recueil Électronique des Sociétés et des Associations (RESA).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum subscribed capital for a Société en Commandite Spéciale (SCSp); capital is freely fixed by the partnership agreement, may be contributed in cash or in kind, and may be partially paid-in as agreed; no escrow or blocked bank account is required by law.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the first meeting of the general partner and the initial limited partners of the Société en Commandite Spéciale (SCSp) hereby: (1) APPROVES and adopts the partnership agreement (contrat de société) in final form. (2) SUBSCRIBES the initial partnership interests and fixes the partnership capital at EUR [·], fully paid-in and subject to no statutory escrow requirement. (3) ADOPTS the registered office at [street address], Luxembourg. (4) APPOINTS [name] as managing partner (gérant), with management authority and sole signature power on bank and registry filings. (5) AUTHORISES the gérant to file the deed with the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register, arrange RESA publication and UBO registration, and open a corporate bank account. (6) DELEGATES counsel to complete ancillary filings. This resolution is effective immediately.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Legal Drafting and Name Pre-Clearance of the Partnership Agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg counsel (avocat) or RCS-accredited filing agent; LBR name search portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Instruct Luxembourg counsel to perform a name availability check via the LBR name reservation tool and to draft the partnership agreement in French or German. The draft must contain the SCSp legal form, the registered office in Luxembourg, the general partner's unlimited liability, limited partners' contribution and profit share, and a corporate object clause limited to professional multilingual translation and media dubbing (ISIC 7490). Coordinate with the future general partner on signature powers and control rights.
required_dossiers: Three proposed entity names in order of preference
Passport or EU ID of each natural-person initial partner and beneficial owner
Proof of residential address of each natural-person partner
Latest constitutional documents of any corporate general partner
Draft partnership agreement (French or German)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the proposed name is refused for identity conflict, resubmit with the next available alternative name or obtain a written coexistence waiver from the prior rights holder.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution and Formalization of the Incorporation Deed
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg notary public (for notarial format) or RCS private-deed regime
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Execute the partnership agreement either before a Luxembourg notary or by private deed with authenticated signatures of all partners. Where a partner is a legal entity, deliver its board resolution authorizing the participation. Verify that no capital duty or registration tax is payable, and that the SCSp's capital clause is validly stated in EUR. If the general partner is an individual, confirm no legal incapacity and no prior bankruptcy disqualification.
required_dossiers: Signed partnership agreement (notarial or private deed)
Signature authentication copies or notarial certificates
Power of attorney for any proxy signatory
Corporate partner's board resolution or consent
Identity documents of all signatories
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary or the RCS accepts only notarial deeds, re-execute the deed before a Luxembourg notary; if signature authentication is challenged, obtain certified copies or legalize signatures by apostille as required.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) via Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) e-filing portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the executed partnership agreement and prescribed annexes electronically through LBR's e-filing platform or deposit physically at the RCS counter. Complete the registration form identifying the general partner and the appointed gérant. Pay the LBR filing tariff electronically. Upon validation, the RCS issues the certificate of registration and assigns the Luxembourg matricule number. Immediately request publication of the incorporation notice in the RESA official electronic gazette.
required_dossiers: Executed incorporation deed (original)
Registration application form for the SCSp
Acceptance of the registered office by the landlord
Identification document of the gérant and general partner
Declaration of good repute for individual general partner
Proof of payment of the LBR filing fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS issues a query or rectification notice, file the supplementary annexes (certified French or German translations, updated powers of attorney, or corrected registered-office acceptance) within the cure period stated in the notice.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within one month of RCS registration, file the beneficial owner declaration through LBR's secure e-UBO service. Declare all natural persons who ultimately own more than 25% of the partnership interests, control the SCSp by other means, or control the general partner. Provide precise percentages and describe the control chain. Retain the RBE acknowledgement for the bank KYC file.
required_dossiers: RCS registration certificate and matricule number
UBO identification form (name, date of birth, nationality, passport copy)
Organizational chart and control-chain description
Statement of partnership interest percentages held by each UBO
Entry in any corporate register of the corporate general partner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the declaration is rejected or suspended due to inaccurate control percentages, reconcile the control matrix with the partnership agreement and refile corrected data through the e-UBO portal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax, VAT and Social Security Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT); Centre Commun de la Sécurité Sociale (CCSS) where applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the electronic registration application to AEDT using the RCS extract and matricule. The SCSp, as a fiscally transparent partnership, obtains its own matricule and, if taxable local activity is carried on, a Luxembourg VAT number, with standard VAT rate verification. No net wealth tax or capital duty is due at formation. If payroll or employees will be engaged, register the SCSp as an employer with the CCSS.
required_dossiers: RCS certificate of registration not older than three months
Final signed partnership agreement
UBO declaration confirmation from the RBE
Identification of the gérant and the general partner
Planned activity declaration for multilingual translation and media dubbing
Corporate bank account details (IBAN)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If AEDT requests further documentation, deliver a fresh RCS extract and a French or German version of the partnership agreement; if the CCSS registration is queried, submit a precise employment-start date and payroll forecast.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Bank Account Opening and AML/KYC Onboarding for Payment Rails
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg-regulated credit institution or payment institution supervised by the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a corporate bank account in the SCSp's name with a CSSF-regulated institution that supports modern international payment rails, including Wise B2B and Payoneer. Present the formation KYC file, complete the source-of-funds and source-of-wealth declarations, and submit a concise business plan demonstrating the localization agency's activities, expected counterparties, and invoicing flows. Complete the customer due diligence at the standard Low-Risk AML tier applicable to professional services.
required_dossiers: RCS certificate and articles of association of the SCSp
UBO extract from the Luxembourg RBE
Passport or ID of authorized signatories and UBOs
Source of funds and source of wealth declaration
Business plan covering multilingual translation and media dubbing services
Projected payment volumes and target rails (Wise B2B, Payoneer)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requires enhanced due diligence, provide a detailed localization-services revenue forecast, pro-forma client agreements, and documentary evidence of the group structure and intended payment flows.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable — professional multilingual translation and media dubbing (ISIC 7490) is an office-based services activity; no industrial operating license is issued by the Luxembourg Ministry of the Economy for this scope.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable — no permis d'exploitation, manufacturing license, or classified-installation operating permit is required for a localization and media dubbing agency.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — office-based translation and dubbing activities do not meet the Annex I or Annex II thresholds of the amended Luxembourg Law of 15 June 2004 on environmental impact assessment; no EIA notification or full EIA report is required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable — no industrial wastewater discharge, VOC emissions, or hazardous waste handling arises from the activities. Any office waste must comply with the national waste management rules in the amended Law of 21 March 2017 on waste management, and any studio sound emissions must respect the general Luxembourg noise control provisions applicable to non-classified premises.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate from the Administration des services de secours (ASS) prior to first occupation of the registered office; first-occupancy conformity certificate confirming structural load capacity, electrical installation safety, and accessibility; and workplace inspection by the Inspection du Travail et des Mines (ITM) where staff are engaged on the premises.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Income and corporate tax: Administration des Contributions Directes (ACD), Luxembourg Inland Revenue, official portal: impotsdirects.public.lu; VAT, registration duties and indirect taxes: Administration de l'Enregistrement, des Domaines et de la TVA (AEDT), official portal: aed.public.lu; single digital public-administration access: MyGuichet.lu (espace entreprises); company registration: Luxembourg Business Registers (RCSL/LBR), official portal: lbr.lu; national identification/matricule issuance: Centre des Technologies de l'Information de l'Etat (CTIE).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For the non-resident-owned LU_SCSP: (1) execute the SCSp partnership agreement before a Luxembourg notary (no minimum capital required) and file it electronically with the RCSL via LBR; (2) obtain the Luxembourg national business number (matricule) from CTIE upon RCSL publication; (3) appoint a Luxembourg tax representative (intermédiaire fiscal agréé) where the entity is established outside the EU, or rely on an EU-established general partner for self-registration; (4) file AEDT VAT registration form (Formulaire 640 TVA) with the partnership agreement, RCSL extract, powers of attorney, partner identity documents and anticipated turnover statement, and receive the Luxembourg VAT identification number in the format LU followed by 8 digits; (5) file the ACD application for the fiscal reference number and complete the annual partnership information return for purely transparent treatment where the SCSp maintains no Luxembourg permanent establishment; (6) optionally request a binding advance tax ruling from the Commission des Avis de l'Administration (CAA) confirming fiscal transparency, non-resident partner PE attribution, and treaty eligibility; (7) register with the Centre Commun de la Sécurité Sociale (CCSS) only where Luxembourg-resident employees are engaged; (8) activate MyGuichet electronic channels for VAT Model 1 returns, EC Sales Lists, OSS filings, and the export documentation register.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible — the Société en Commandite Spéciale (SCSp) has no separate legal personality and is statutorily fiscally transparent for Luxembourg corporate income tax (IRC), municipal business tax (ICT) and net wealth tax (ISF). All translation, dubbing, subtitling and localization-agency profits, royalties, capital gains, expenses and credits flow through pro rata to the general and limited partners. Entity-level taxation is not applicable; territorial scope is effectively global for Luxembourg-connected income, and no tax-exempt zone regime applies. A Luxembourg permanent establishment is attributed to every foreign partner when the SCSp carries on its multilingual localization business through a fixed place of business in Luxembourg, triggering Luxembourg reach-through taxation under Article 175 LIR for non-resident partners.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Luxembourg does not operate a US-style check-the-box election; entity classification is statutory. Available mechanisms: (i) binding CAA advance tax ruling confirming pass-through treatment, PE attribution and income-tax treaty eligibility for foreign partners; (ii) VAT grouping election ('assujetti unique') effective 1 January 2025 permitting the SCSp to consolidate with a Luxembourg SOPARFI or taxable affiliate for VAT purposes; (iii) voluntary VAT registration despite the EUR 35,000 small-business exemption (Article 57 LTVAG) so as to recover input VAT on production costs, dubbing equipment and software; (iv) OSS (One-Stop-Shop) election for intra-EU B2C supplies of e-services and digital media to avoid multiple non-resident VAT registrations; (v) alignment of the SCSp's transparent characterization with foreign anti-hybrid regimes (ATAD 2) to prevent double non-taxation or double deduction outcomes; (vi) optional reporting election to treat the partnership as a non-taxable entity for Luxembourg withholding-tax purposes where all partners are non-residents and no Luxembourg PE arises.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms_continued: No other entity-level elections are available; the SCSp cannot opt for opaque corporate taxation, and no hybrid check-the-box designing is possible within Luxembourg domestic law.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL) is the central bank and the official repository for external statistics and monetary operations. Luxembourg maintains no separate foreign-exchange control administration; the Ministry of Finance and the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) oversee account-opening compliance and financial-sanctions enforcement respectively.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Luxembourg is a euro-area Member State and applies the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union free-movement-of-capital regime (Articles 63–65). Both current-account and capital-account payments are fully convertible and freely remittable in any permitted currency. Profit remittance from an SCSp is not subject to exchange-control approval: the SCSp is fiscally transparent and distributions to partners are treated as partnership allocations, not dividends. The practical remittance hurdles are exclusively bank-side AML/KYC proof obligations, EU financial-sanctions screening, and the requirement that the SCSp maintain up-to-date beneficial-ownership records in the Luxembourg Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Not applicable. Luxembourg law imposes no surrender requirement, no mandatory conversion ratio, no prescribed repatriation window, and no BCL approval for export-related receipts. Cross-border payments above statistical thresholds are reported by resident banks under ECB/BCL external-statistics rules, but the SCSp itself has no filing obligation for routine trade receipts.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (Spuerkees / BCEE)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Low for primary settlement or escrow continuity; Medium for ancillary disbursement-only workflows. Wise Business and Payoneer may be used as convenient output rails, but they are payment institutions, not Luxembourg licensed credit institutions, and their non-EEA segregated accounts cannot host Luxembourg IBANs or receive statutory escrow balances. A PSD2 passport from another EEA state is acceptable for payment services, yet the SCSp must maintain a principal settlement account at a Luxembourg bank or an EU/EEA credit institution and must ensure that every cross-border flow is traceable back to the KYC-complete SCSp and its beneficial owners.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For an SCSp with non-resident partners, Luxembourg banks generally require an in-person or equivalent video-identification interview with the managing officer of the general partner and with every natural-person beneficial owner holding 25% or more. Remote onboarding is legally permitted under eIDAS-compliant qualified electronic signature and video-identification procedures, but in practice a fully remote opening is rare for a partnership structure; appointing a Luxembourg-registered authorised signatory or agent materially accelerates onboarding.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opaque partnership ownership structure and silent limited partners in the SCSp
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified copy of the limited partnership agreement (contrat de société), RCS/LBR constitution extract, complete partner register with ownership percentages and economic entitlements, current RBE extract, UBO declaration for each natural-person partner, passport copies, proof of residential address, corporate charters and board resolutions for corporate limited partners.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source-of-funds concerns for initial capital injection and subsequent partner distributions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Twelve months of bank statements for each contributing partner, historical tax returns, executed financing or loan agreements, sale-and-purchase contracts explaining prior accumulation of wealth, notarised source-of-wealth declaration, and a written undertaking that no cash or third-party anonymous funds are used.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear commercial substance of the multilingual translation and media-dubbing activity
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed client localization contracts or letters of intent, vendor/subcontractor agreements for translation and dubbing services, a projected transaction schedule, sample invoices, a detailed business plan showing addressable markets, pricing methodology, and expected monthly turnover.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions, export-control, or restricted-media exposure through global clients and intellectual-property royalties
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Negative sanctions-screening reports for all counterparties and ultimate clients, end-use attestation letters, a media-rights confirmation matrix, an export-control or dual-use applicability opinion from Luxembourg counsel, and a no-conflict legal opinion where intellectual-property or royalty flows are part of the revenue model.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Use of non-Luxembourg digital EMIs and alternative payment rails alongside the core bank account
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A written treasury policy approved by the general partner governing ancillary rails, the bank consent letter covering Wise/Payoneer usage, KYC records for each EMI account, a full funds-flow mapping from the Luxembourg settlement account to final beneficiaries, and reconciliation ledgers showing that EMI balances are never used as a storage vehicle.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital contributions from non-resident partners are remitted by SWIFT MT103 or SEPA transfer into the SCSp's EUR account at a Luxembourg credit institution. The remittance information should state: 'Capital contribution to SCSp', identify the beneficiary as the Luxembourg-resident partnership, and include the partnership's RCS number. No BCL approval is required; the receiving bank will assign the appropriate balance-of-payments classification for external statistics. The bank must be provided with the executed capital commitment schedule and a board/general-partner resolution authorising the account to receive funds before the first transfer.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound settlement for localization services is executed through the Luxembourg bank as instructing bank. EUR payments within the EEA use SEPA Credit Transfer or TARGET2; non-EEA and non-EUR payments use SWIFT MT103 with robust remittance information such as invoice number, contract reference, and commercial purpose. For high-value production milestones or when counterparties require bank confirmation, an irrevocable documentary letter of credit (Commercial L/C) or SWIFT gpi tracked payment is used. Trade disbursements may be made in USD, EUR, CNY, or other freely convertible currencies without BCL authorisation, but each outward payment remains subject to sanctions screening and to the bank's internal fraud controls.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright FX forwards between EUR and USD, GBP, CHF, CNY, or JPY executed with a Luxembourg/EU credit institution
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for currencies with local convertibility constraints
Cross-currency swaps (EUR versus USD, GBP, CHF, or other major currencies) under ISDA/CSA documentation
FX swaps used for short-dated settlement-liquidity management
Vanilla FX call and put options for purchase of trade settlement currencies
Currency futures traded on Eurex or other EU regulated markets where approved by the SCSp's treasury policy

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of beneficial ownership (RBE declaration)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (Registre des Beneficiaires Effectifs, RBE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Anniversary-based: within 30 days after the anniversary date of the initial RBE registration; thereafter on each successive annual confirmation cycle
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Criminal fine of EUR 1,250 to EUR 125,000 and/or imprisonment up to 5 years for intentional non-compliance; separate administrative delay penalties may be imposed by the Luxembourg Business Registers; persistent default is recorded publicly and blocks distributions

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts filing with the RCS (unless validly exempted as a non-legal-person SCSp or if the partnership agreement does not require RCS publication)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (Registre de Commerce et des Societes, RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 7 months after the end of the financial year; for a 31 December year-end, filing deadline is 31 July
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers a formal notice followed by judicial penalty payments (astreinte) of approximately EUR 100 per day and possible court-ordered strike-off of the RCS registration; directors or general partners may be held liable for damages

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual maintenance and verification of commercial register data (registered office, general partner, managers, statutory representatives)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No fixed calendar deadline; mandatory update within 1 month after any change in registered office, partnership agreement, managers, liquidators, or constitutional documents; annual verification is performed as part of the UBO confirmation and annual accounts cycle
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file statutorily required changes within 1 month may lead to criminal fines and a judicial order to rectify the register; continued non-compliance may support administrative strike-off proceedings

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A Luxembourg SCSp has no legal personality and therefore has no statutory audit requirement at entity level. A mandatory independent audit arises only where the partnership agreement or an investor undertaking requires a reviseur d'entreprises agree, where the SCSp is a regulated alternative investment vehicle, or where the general partner is a Luxembourg commercial entity exceeding the Law of 19 December 2002 thresholds: two of three criteria being balance-sheet total above EUR 4.4 million, net turnover above EUR 8.8 million, and average headcount above 50 employees.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP under the Law of 19 December 2002 and the Law of 10 August 1915 on commercial companies; IFRS is permitted where required by investors or for consolidated reporting, while statutory RCS filings, if applicable, follow Luxembourg GAAP.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The SCSp must file its initial UBO declaration before or concurrently with RCS registration, update the RBE file within one month of any change in beneficial ownership, and annually confirm the correctness of the RBE data within the anniversary-based confirmation window. Each confirmation must be signed by a partner or manager and certify the current ultimate owners, taking into account transferred partnership interests, control chains, voting rights, and any other indirect ownership mechanisms.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of limited partners and partnership interests
Register of general partners, managers and statutory representatives
Minute book of partner and management resolutions
Supporting UBO ownership-chain and KYC documentation

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24.94% aggregate Luxembourg corporate income tax rate (17.00% corporate income tax plus 7.00% unemployment fund surcharge plus 6.75% solidarity surcharge plus 0.25% state tax surcharge for the 2025 tax year; local trade tax excluded)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: SCSp treated as fiscally transparent partnership: no Luxembourg CIT at entity level; income and gains attributed to partners. Parent-subsidiary participation exemption available where corporate partners hold at least 10% participation or EUR 1.2 million acquisition cost for 12 months. No statutory tax holiday for translation/localization agency; standard deductions for employment costs and IP amortization are available.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Model 560G (for fiscally transparent partnerships and integrated groups) or Model 560E for non-resident corporate filers; electronic filing mandatory via MyGuichet.lu / eCDF (Electronic Data Collection and Filing) system with LU CSRF authentication token and RBE accreditation for approved fiduciary agents.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Standard deadline is 31 December of the calendar year following the fiscal year-end, extended to 28/29 February of the second following year without penalty for e-filers holding a valid business license; SCSp fiscal year defaults to calendar year unless a different business year is authorized by the Luxembourg tax administration (AEDT).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Identification of the SCSp: name, RCSL registration number, RBE identification number, registered office address, and correspondent tax number (matricule d'imposition).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident corporate or fund partners must provide their foreign tax identification number and country of residence; the SCSp must file only if it is the direct taxable person for withheld taxes, otherwise each partner files an individual Luxembourg return proportional to their share.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Confirmation of fiscal transparency election and allocation of taxable results among partners: percentage interests, profit/loss participation, capital accounts, and any special allocation agreements.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Partners should ensure the Luxembourg filing entity is not the taxable subject; each non-resident partner must evidence entitlement to treaty benefits via Luxembourg DTA partner state status before claiming transparency treatment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Commercial result as per Luxembourg GAAP (comptes annuels) before tax: revenues from translation, subtitling, dubbing, linguistic review, localization project management, and media adaptation services.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident SCSp must attach Luxembourg statutory accounts in EUR; if the entity is deemed a foreign permanent establishment of a Luxembourg partner, allocate Luxembourg-source revenue to a Luxembourg branch schedule.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Non-deductible expenses and disallowed items: fines, penalties, excessive remuneration to managing partners without substance, inadequate transfer pricing adjustments, and non-documented management fees.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Add back amounts charged by foreign affiliated localization agents that failed the arm's length standard or the formal invoicing requirement of Article 57 LIR.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Exceptional and non-recurring items, including provisions, impairment write-downs on receivables from dubbing studios, and exchange gains or losses from Wise/Payoneer multi-currency accounts.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Provide exchange rate source certificates for cross-border payment rail accounts and avoid rolling revaluation of intercompany payables without a documented forex policy.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable base before loss carryforward after application of tax transparency and exclusion of partner-level income streams.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the SCSp has a separate Luxembourg withholding obligation on Luxembourg-source patent or copyright royalties, ensure this line aligns with the agreed partner allocation schedule.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Available tax losses carried forward from prior fiscal years (maximum five years for Luxembourg corporate income tax purposes).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners claiming losses from a Luxembourg transparent SCSp against Luxembourg-source income must prove the SCSp is not in anti-loss-shell status and that the partner has taxable Luxembourg nexus.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Partners' gross income allocated from the SCSp for Luxembourg individual or corporate income tax reporting, including directors' remuneration if the managing partner is a Luxembourg tax resident.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners report only Luxembourg-source income derived through the SCSp and complete form 770-DTA for treaty relief; no residence-country remittance basis applies to Luxembourg-source commercial income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Withholding tax summary, if applicable: Luxembourg withholding taxes on director fees, copyright royalties, or interest paid by the SCSp to non-resident partners.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Withholding at 15% on interest (unless treaty reduced) and 15% on royalties must be recorded; DTA relief may be claimed ex post through the Luxembourg refund procedure (RIC form).

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late e-filing triggers an automatic late penalty between EUR 50 and EUR 200 for the first month and further monthly penalties up to EUR 500; failure to file after formal notice may yield a disciplinary fine (amende) of up to EUR 25,000 per missing declaration. Interest on late tax payments accrues at 0.8% per month (9.6% annualized) on unpaid CIT balances; intentional non-filing can lead to tax evasion fines of EUR 10,000 plus criminal imprisonment terms of 8 days to 5 years for the filing officer.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15% statutory Luxembourg dividend withholding tax; because the SCSp is fiscally transparent, profit distributions to partners are not characterized as dividends at the SCSp level and no 15% withholding tax is levied on the SCSp itself. If a Luxembourg corporate partner re-distributes profits, the standard 15% dividend withholding tax applies, subject to the 100% Luxembourg participation exemption.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke treaty relief, the non-resident partner must be considered the beneficial owner of the SCSp income. The partner must obtain a valid Luxembourg certificate of residence (form 770D-TA) or a foreign tax residence certificate (TRC) issued by the treaty partner's tax authority, certify no treaty abuse under LIR Article 233 (subject-to-tax clause), and submit a reduced withholding refund claim via form RIC (remboursement d'impôt de retenue) to the Luxembourg direct contributions office (Administration des contributions directes). The SCSp itself must maintain an up-to-date register of partners, capital accounts, and distribution minutes; authorities may require substance evidence such as annual reports, local bank/seats, and actual localization-service operations in Luxembourg.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: 15% Luxembourg statutory withholding tax; DTA rate is typically 0-10% under most Luxembourg treaties (e.g., 0% under the Luxembourg-US DTA for copyright royalties, 5% under several EU treaties; the interest rate is generally 10% for EU source interest under domestic law, 0% under the EU Interest and Royalty Directive if the affiliate holds a 25% direct shareholding and meets the common tax fraud test; treaty rates under Luxembourg DTAs are usually 0% for bank interest and 5-10% for commercial interest). For an SCSp, interest and royalty paid to non-resident partners are subject to Luxembourg withholding only when the SCSp is treated as the debtor of record and the partner is the beneficial owner; otherwise the transparency principle overrides.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 500,000 annual related-party transactions in goods or services triggers mandatory Luxembourg Local File and Master File documentation obligation; intra-group service charges exceeding EUR 100,000 per year require a documented service agreement and demonstrate no duplication of shareholder costs; all Luxembourg SCSp entities must maintain contemporaneous TP documentation regardless of revenue if cross-border related-party payments are made.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP, Resale Price, Cost Plus, TNMM, Profit Split
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Although Luxembourg has not enacted full Economic Substance Regulations equivalent to the UAE ESR regime, the doctrine applies through the LIR general anti-abuse rule, the EU Anti-Tax Avoidance Directive (ATAD) substance requirements, the OECD BEPS Action 5 substantial activity requirement for preferential regimes, and judicial doctrines (e.g., dual-residence and conduit-company principles). An SCSp active in multilingual localization must demonstrate substantive local activity: qualified management decisions in Luxembourg, employees or directors with actual localization industry expertise, physical office, and rejection of passive letterbox status. Failure to demonstrate substance may trigger denial of treaty benefits, exchange of information under OECD/Global Forum, and retrograde reclassification as a fully taxable Luxembourg company on distributed income.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Intentionally omitting localization agency revenue derived from Wise/Payoneer payment rails, failing to file the annual Luxembourg tax return, or presenting fabricated dubbing/subtitling supplier invoices to reduce taxable profit.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal fine of EUR 10,000 up to EUR 250,000 (doubled for professionals), payment of all evaded tax plus 0.8% monthly default interest, and imprisonment of 8 days to 5 years under LIR Article 395 and LIR Article 396; automatic forfeiture of any claimed losses.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and managing partners who signed false declarations are jointly and severally liable for the corporate tax debt under LIR Article 109. Civil managers risk personal bankruptcy proceedings, freezing of intercompany accounts, and travel bans issued by Luxembourg tax authorities; custodial sentence cannot be waived by company liquidation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the SCSp solely as a conduit to invoice multilingual translation services to a Portuguese sister localization agency without Luxembourg staff, real office, or business decision-making, while claiming Luxembourg treaty benefits on royalties or dividends.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Reclassification of the SCSp as a fully taxable Luxembourg resident company; denial of treaty benefits with retroactive re-assessed tax up to 6 years; administrative fine up to EUR 100,000 under the Luxembourg general anti-abuse rule (ATAD Article 6) and possible removal from the Luxembourg trade register (RCSL) as an inactive shell.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Courts may pierce the corporate veil under civil/company law doctrine when the SCSp is an artificial arrangement; directors are personally liable for the entirety of tax arrears, restitution of distributions, and damages to creditors. Directors of shell conduits face director disqualification for 10 years and exit bans if criminal misrepresentation is found.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Charging below-market or above-market rates to affiliated localization affiliates (e.g., a Luxembourg SCSp billing its US parent EUR 5,000 per hour for translation coordination services) without benchmarking, or failing to file the Luxembourg TP documentation when the EUR 500,000 threshold is exceeded.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Primary TP adjustment increasing taxable income; secondary penalty of 5% to 25% of the adjustment amount (Article 56 LIR applies arm's length principle; late-payment interest of 0.8% per month on the reassessed tax); administrative fines up to EUR 50,000 for documentation failure; correlative adjustments require mutual agreement procedure under DTA.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Managing partners who approved the non-arm's-length invoices may be held jointly liable for the deficit, particularly if they drew distributions while knowing the intercompany pricing was not defensible; a Luxembourg criminal court may impose a personal fine of EUR 12,500 per false document.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Failure to File Tax Return and Administrative Offence
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Missing the 31 December/February filing deadline for three consecutive fiscal years or refusing to file after formal warning letters.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Daily penalty of EUR 50 per day of delay, capped at 10% of the assessed tax; ex officio taxation by AEDT; exclusion of deductions and expenses not documented; loss of loss-carryforward eligibility; a coercive fine (astreinte) of up to EUR 2,500 per day until the return is completed.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The AEDT may issue a personal collection order against the fiduciary or managing partner for the penalty charges; directors receive personal liability notices and may be subject to bank garnishment for the SCSp's tax debts if the non-filing constitutes gross negligence.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Anti-Money Laundering / Financial Crime in Cross-Border Payments
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to perform KYC on the ultimate beneficial owners of the SCSp; accepting undisclosed cash or third-party settlement from foreign media localization clients; or using Wise/Payoneer rails to split invoice amounts to avoid generating a Luxembourg audit trail.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: AML law of 12 November 2004 (as amended) imposes administrative fines up to EUR 1,000,000 and criminal fines up to EUR 5,000,000; asset freezing orders; prohibition against the fund manager; removal from RCSL; report to the Financial Intelligence Unit is mandatory.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: AML obligations attach to partners of an SCSp acting as fiduciaries; non-compliance triggers personal criminal liability, confiscation of profits derived through the payment corridors, director disqualification, and a travel ban where a flight risk is proven.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Incorrect Withholding Tax on Cross-Border Interest/Royalties
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: SCSp pays a copyright royalty for multilingual dubbing software to a non-resident partner without withholding 15% and without verifying the EU Interest/Royalty Directive or DTA reduction.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The withholding tax is deemed to have been received but not collected; the tax authority levies a fine of 100% of the un-withheld tax, plus 0.8% monthly interest; the debtor/SCSp is exclusively liable for the grossed-up tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The managing partner who approved the payment without verifying a valid TRC is personally liable for the withheld amount; Luxembourg criminal courts may classify the failure as willful breach leading to a EUR 25,000 fine and a custodial sentence of up to 3 years.
